title: How Planets Form
description: Planets grow in the disk of gas and dust about a young star. Dust sticks into pebbles, pebbles into planetesimals, and where the disk is heavy enough it can break straight into clumps: whether it does is told by Toomre's Q, its pressure and spin against its own gravity. The first solids still survive in meteorites: chondrules, droplets melted in flashes, and calcium-aluminium-rich inclusions, which lead-lead dating puts at 4.567 billion years, the age of the solar system. The Protoplanetary Disk lies in the Accretion Frontier.

puzzle.goal: A disk of surface density Σ, sound speed cs and epicyclic frequency κ resists collapsing into clumps by pressure and by spin. Write Toomre's Q: below 1 it breaks up.
puzzle.name: Toomre parameter
puzzle.ask: Find Q for cs = @{cs} m/s, κ = 2e-7 /s, Σ = 1700 kg/m² and G = 6.674e-11.
puzzle.method: A ring of size λ collapses if πGΣ beats both the pressure (cs²/λ) and the spin (κ²λ); the worst case gives Q = csκ/πGΣ.
